### workspace go --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace go [REF | "TEXT"] [--workflow ID] [--input KEY=VALUE]... [--here] [--text] [--base REF] [--dry-run] [--json]

Start a workflow with one argument. A ticket, pull request, issue or branch is the ref; text with a space
is free text that names a new branch, unless it holds one pull request, issue or ticket (see below).
Free text always makes a new worktree workspace off the default branch,
even from inside a worktree workspace; --here runs it in this checkout instead. A ref makes or reuses its worktree
workspace, as `workflow start` does, unless it is the branch you are on; bare `workspace go` runs here too, in a
linked worktree workspace off the default branch. go never runs on the default branch or the main checkout's
branch. It prints the workflow it chose and why (--workflow, then workflows.by_ref.KIND, workflows.default,
then built in: pr-feedback for a pull request, else rpiv) before it acts. A sentence that holds one pull
request, issue or ticket (a key in uppercase) is read as that ref, with the sentence as the task; --text keeps it plain.

        --workflow ID                Use this workflow instead of the configured one
        --input KEY=VALUE            Set a workflow input; repeatable
        --here                       Run free text in this worktree workspace instead of making a new one; refused where go can't run in place
        --text                       Treat the quoted sentence as plain text; find no ticket, pull request or issue in it
        --base REF                   Start a new branch from this branch, tag or commit instead of the default branch; refused when go runs in place
        --dry-run                    Check everything and create nothing
        --json                       Print one JSON document; other output goes to stderr
    -h, --help                       Show this help

Examples:
  workspace go PROJ-123    # a ticket: make or reuse its worktree workspace and start the chosen workflow
  workspace go "try the thing"    # free text: a new branch named from it, in a new worktree workspace, even from inside one
  workspace go --text "fix the login timeout from PROJ-123"    # plain text: a new branch named from it, nothing read as a ticket
  workspace go --here "try the thing"    # in a worktree workspace off the default branch: run the workflow here, with the text as the task
  workspace go    # in a worktree workspace off the default branch: run the workflow here
  workspace go "try the thing" --base origin/main    # start the new branch from origin's main, when the local default branch may be behind
  workspace go fix-login --workflow investigate --dry-run    # check a branch with a named workflow, create nothing
  workspace go "try the thing" --input task="Try the thing" --json    # scripted, with a workflow input
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace go --bogus
--- exit 1
--- stdout
--- stderr

--- end
